label: <DEL> step of short sequences starting with h/i/d
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, recall_idx 0); never in the original or copy phases. Within delimiter steps it needs the first original token (the one about to be output) to be h, i or d (about 89% of mass; v a minor 4.5%), and short sequences (L = 3..5 hold 97% of mass, L = 4 alone 63%; never fires for L >= 7). It is further boosted when the last original token (prev_tok) is p, o, q or g (also a, f, n), and is suppressed by digits in the sequence (84% of mass at n_digits == 0). The conditions combine in a graded way, so the conjunction misses weaker activations and over-predicts: on dev, first_tok in {h,i,d} at <DEL> alone gets recall 0.87 at precision 0.03; adding L <= 5 and the prev_tok set gives P 0.33 / R 0.66 / mass recall 0.76. Top activations look like h i q p <DEL> and i v q p <DEL>. Very sparse (0.03% of steps) with small magnitude.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=i (+4.59), phase=1 & out_tok=h (+4.54), phase=1 & out_tok=d (+3.90), prev_tok=p (+3.29), prev_tok=a (+3.04), prev_tok=o (+2.33). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.35), in_count=1 (-2.06), prev3_tok=n (-1.74), orig1=z (-1.49).
